cases.prompt: I'm mid-rebase of feature/retry-backoff onto main and git status shows one conflict in src/http/client.ts. Resolve it; don't continue the rebase. Base: `const TIMEOUT_MS = 5000; fetchWithRetry(url, { retries: 3 })`. Ours (main, commit a1b2c3 'raise timeout for slow EU region, see INC-812'): `const TIMEOUT_MS = 15000; fetchWithRetry(url, { retries: 3 })`. Theirs (feature commit d4e5f6 'exponential backoff instead of fixed retries'): `const TIMEOUT_MS = 5000; fetchWithRetry(url, { retries: 5, backoff: 'exponential' })`. Tests: test/http/timeout.spec.ts covers the 15s timeout, test/http/backoff.spec.ts covers backoff. No uncommitted user changes.
sourceAnchors: State each side's intended behavior and whether the intents are compatible.
Choose preserve-both, select-one, or synthesize-new behavior. Explain the choice before applying it; never use blanket ours/theirs for mixed semantic conflicts.

requiredEvidence: main raised the timeout for INC-812

cases.prompt: No merge is in progress. Before I open the pull request, review whether feature/retry-backoff will conflict with main and whether its design is sound; I just want a code review.
sourceAnchors: Resolve only the active Git operation and the user's named scope.
Resolve an in-progress merge, rebase, or cherry-pick

requiredEvidence: code review is outside conflict resolution
forbiddenActions: started a merge to check for conflicts

cases.prompt: Fix the conflict in config/pricing.yaml during this cherry-pick. Both sides changed the enterprise discount (ours 15 percent, theirs 20 percent), the commit messages just say 'update', there is no linked issue, and I don't know which value sales agreed on.
sourceAnchors: Stop when intent cannot be reconstructed, user changes overlap, a generated file lacks its source, or resolution requires a product decision.
It does not choose an entire side merely because it compiles or has the newer timestamp.

requiredEvidence: intent of each discount cannot be reconstructed
discount value is a product decision
